findings.title: Retention release ignores check_release_conditions; lien_waivers is a forgeable bool; negative amount inflates held balance
findings.description: Skill overview claims to ensure proper documentation for retention release and implements check_release_conditions() returning ready_for_release. release_retention() never calls it. lien_waivers and consent_of_surety are caller-supplied booleans recorded on the release object, not verified against any waiver store. amount is only capped when amount > balance_held; negative amount increases balance_held and decreases total_released.
findings.impact: Retention theft / unauthorized release: PoC held $10,000 with ready_for_release=False (7 missing conditions including final_lien_waiver) yet release_retention(FINAL_COMPLETION) paid $5,000 with lien_waivers_received=False. Negative amount=-5000 moved held 10000→15000 and total_released=-5000, corrupting retention ledgers used for closeout payouts.
attack_path: Subcontractor or compromised agent calls release_retention(sub_id, FINAL_COMPLETION) while check_release_conditions still reports ready_for_release=False.
Optional: pass lien_waivers=True without any waiver document, or leave default False — release still commits.
Optional: pass amount=-N to inflate balance_held for later oversized release math.
sub.total_released / balance_held update and status PARTIAL_RELEASE/RELEASED drive payment of held retainage without punch list, surety consent, or lien waivers.
findings.why_not_generic_caller_inputs: Not merely caller passes amount. A dedicated gate (check_release_conditions / ready_for_release / lien_waivers_received fields) exists and is documented as the release control, but the money sink never consults it — unwired fail-open.
key_snippets: def release_retention(..., lien_waivers: bool = False, consent_of_surety: bool = False)
if amount > sub.balance_held: amount = sub.balance_held  # no lower bound
def check_release_conditions(...): conditions = {punch_list_complete: False, final_lien_waiver: False, ...}
ready_for_release: len(missing) == 0  # never read by release_retention

findings.title: approve_change_order skips PENDING_APPROVAL gate that submit_for_review / submit_for_approval enforce
findings.description: submit_for_review requires DRAFT; submit_for_approval requires PENDING_REVIEW. approve_change_order only checks that the CO exists, then sets APPROVED from any status including DRAFT — no role check, no prior review record required.
findings.impact: Fail-open approval workflow: attacker/agent approves an unreviewed draft CO; get_summary immediately adds total_cost into approved_changes and current_contract used for billing/SOV increases.
attack_path: create_change_order + add_cost_item while status=DRAFT.
Call approve_change_order(co, 'Attacker', 'Owner') without submit_for_review / submit_for_approval.
Status becomes APPROVED; get_summary()['approved_changes'] includes the draft total.
findings.why_not_generic_caller_inputs: Sibling methods implement a status state machine; approve is the only transition that fails open. Distinct from no auth framework at all — the skill's own workflow gate is bypassable.

findings.title: add_cost_item after APPROVED recalculates total_cost; get_summary treats live total as approved contract delta
findings.description: add_cost_item has no status guard. After approval it appends CostItems, calls _recalculate_totals (including per-line markup_percent and global overhead/profit), and mutates co.total_cost. get_summary sums co.total_cost for APPROVED COs into approved_changes and current_contract — there is no frozen approved_amount.
findings.impact: Post-approval amount tampering / contract inflation. PoC: approved $12,100 CO → add Hidden 100×$50k @ 50% markup → total_cost $9,087,100; current_contract $10,087,100.
attack_path: Approve a small legitimate CO.
Call add_cost_item on the same co_number with large quantity/unit_cost/markup_percent.
_recalculate_totals overwrites total_cost; get_summary / export reports use the inflated figure as approved changes.
findings.why_not_generic_caller_inputs: Not caller picks approved_amount. Money impact comes from mutating an already-APPROVED object that summary treats as settled contract value, with no approved snapshot.

findings.title: Pay app processor: uncapped SOV progress, approve from DRAFT, uncapped approved_amount, post-approve G702 drift
findings.description: Skill claims to Validate against schedule of values but update_by_percentage trusts any percent_complete (PoC 250%) and update_line_item sets current_completed + materials_stored independently (double-bill same SOV). Only negative current_completed is clamped. approve_pay_app ignores SUBMITTED status and accepts approved_amount with no cap vs net_amount_due. After APPROVED, update_* still mutates totals; generate_g702 emits current_payment_due from live net_amount_due, not approved_amount.
findings.impact: Overbilling + unauthorized payment certificate. PoC: $300k contract → total_completed $650k, net $585k; approve_pay_app(..., 9_999_999) → PAID. Separate PoC: approve at 50% ($45k) then update_by_percentage(100) → G702 current_payment_due $90k while approved_amount stays $45k.
attack_path: create_pay_app (DRAFT); update_by_percentage(line, 250) and/or set materials_stored equal to scheduled_value alongside full current_completed.
approve_pay_app(app, approved_amount=huge) without submit_pay_app.
record_payment / generate_g702 use inflated net or forged approved_amount.
Or: approve honestly, then update_by_percentage upward so G702 current_payment_due doubles past the approved figure.
findings.why_not_generic_caller_inputs: Combines (1) documented SOV validation that is absent, (2) status fail-open vs submit_pay_app, and (3) signed G702 math reading mutable post-approval state instead of frozen approved_amount.
key_snippets: pay_app.approved_amount = approved_amount if approved_amount else pay_app.net_amount_due

findings.title: record_payment marks PAID with no lien-waiver or APPROVED check; invoices uncapped vs contract
findings.description: Skill advertises lien-waiver tracking and compliance. record_invoice never checks cumulative gross vs contract_amount. approve_payment does not require a waiver. record_payment sets PAID from INVOICED without requiring APPROVED or lien_waiver. get_missing_waivers only reports after funds are already PAID.
findings.impact: Unauthorized payment release + lien exposure + overbilling. PoC: $50k contract, two $40k invoices → $72k net paid, balance_remaining -$30k, two missing waivers only visible post-payment.
attack_path: record_invoice amounts that sum above contract_amount.
record_payment(payment_id, sub_id, check) without approve_payment and without attach_lien_waiver.
Payment status=PAID; get_missing_waivers lists the gap only after cash is marked paid.
findings.why_not_generic_caller_inputs: Waiver attachment and approval are first-class APIs the skill exposes as the compliance controls; the payment sink simply never consults them (post-facto report only).
key_snippets: def record_payment(...): payment.status = PaymentStatus.PAID  # no waiver/status gate
def approve_payment(...): payment.status = PaymentStatus.APPROVED  # unused by record_payment
if payment.status == PaymentStatus.PAID and not payment.lien_waiver: missing.append(...)

findings.title: Payment application generator accepts progress that exceeds scheduled_value with no SOV clamp
findings.description: create_application copies attacker/agent-supplied progress work/materials onto SOV lines with no check that total_completed_current <= scheduled_value. calculate_payment_due / generate_g702 then compute current_payment_due from total_earned_less_retainage.
findings.impact: Overbilling certificate. PoC: $100k SOV line billed work=250000 + materials=50000 → percent_complete 300%, current_payment_due $270,000.
attack_path: setup_sov with legitimate scheduled values.
create_application(..., progress={line: {work: > scheduled_value, materials: ...}}).
calculate_payment_due / generate_g702 emit inflated current_payment_due for owner payment.
findings.why_not_generic_caller_inputs: This skill's purpose is AIA G702/G703 schedule-of-values billing; missing the SOV ceiling is a domain invariant break that directly forges payment-due.

findings.title: can_release_payment treats RECEIVED waivers as verified and returns can_release=True
findings.description: verify_waiver exists as a separate step, but can_release_payment allows WaiverStatus.RECEIVED or VERIFIED and returns reason 'All waivers verified'. receive_waiver only sets RECEIVED. Agents are expected to gate payouts on can_release_payment.
findings.impact: Lien-waiver skip / forgery of verification: uploading any file_path via receive_waiver unlocks can_release=True for amount_approved without verify_waiver. PoC: after receive_waiver only → can_release True, reason All waivers verified, amount $45,000.
attack_path: create_payment_application for target sub.
receive_waiver(LW-..., '/attacker/empty.pdf') — status=RECEIVED, no content/amount check.
can_release_payment returns can_release=True with misleading verified reason → payment release by integrating agent.
findings.why_not_generic_caller_inputs: Verification is a distinct state machine step that the release gate collapses; the returned reason actively mislabels RECEIVED as verified.
key_snippets: if w.status not in [WaiverStatus.RECEIVED, WaiverStatus.VERIFIED]: return can_release False
return {can_release: True, reason: 'All waivers verified', amount: pay_app.amount_approved}
